title: Whispers from the Liminal — ep. 13 · hometown something? (excerpt)

nodes.text: WHISPERS FROM THE LIMINAL · ep. 13 · hometown something? (excerpt)
What does he hope to accomplish?
He's homesick. He wants to go home.
Then let him leave.
You don't understand.
No I don't. Tell me.
I can't. But try to understand this. Suppose you had an opportunity to make a world for yourself. How would you make it?
I don't know. I'm not a god.
But imagine, for a second, that you were. What kind of Eden would you make it?
What are you saying? Are you implying that you're 'Eve' and he's 'Adam'?
NO! Well, not exactly. There was an accident. And I think that everything you see before you- except for me- is a result of that accident.
Desmond shakes his head with a hangman's humor.
Imagine a world with two Gods, two creators with conflicting ideologies and beliefs and superstitions. Imagine them falling from paradise and landing in 'Lynch's Peak', Oregon.
That's insane.
We were young and naive, we pushed the limits of science. We were insane.
So you suggest that my whole universe is nothing more than the immaculate union of-
I don't suggest. I insist. Desmond. I know who you are.
You do? Really? Am I some figment of your imagination?
You were, at one time. But now, you're flesh and blood. Like me.
Alright, Miss Supreme Being, tell me who I am.
Desmond Daniels was a boy I stole glances at in Sunday school.
My last name isn't Daniels.

No, it isn't, but Cooper is. Richard Cooper, Officer Cooper, was a cop. I fell in love with him when I was seventeen. He was tall, dark, and handsome. He died in the line of duty. Hard to imagine in a small town, but it happened. And I was heartbroken.
You can't prove a thing.
Samantha smiles. She opens up the compass on her necklace. Behind it, is a small newspaper clipping. A cop, clean cut, looks very much like Desmond.
His eyes squint in disbelief.
You don't have to believe me. That's quite alright. I just thought you should know, of all people.
